analyticalQuestion: Can the common input slope s/j be retained in the active-tail column so that an all-order convex endpoint theorem replaces the R0.39 termwise loss, certifies the old 0.257 failure probe, and identifies the next bottleneck?
supportedClaim: For each fixed charge 2 through 240, the complete center column is a convex function of x=s/j, so every admissible degree is bounded by the common endpoints x=0 and x=s/J_s, followed by the uniform prefactor (J_s+1)/J_s. Together with the inherited exceptional-charge and large-charge proofs, this covers every charge and every degree above 80. The old 0.257 failure now passes with active-tail bound 0.68048588141014910513. At r=9/32, the all-order active-tail bound is 0.77854233161724448351 and the full two-endpoint transport bound is 0.99621120319950467993, certifying the reduced system. At 141/500=0.282, the active fixed point still passes but the present transport bound is 1.0003750451629852617.
